findings.summary: The bridge's ordinary merge pass treats a fork PR like a branch of the repository: one that names a project ticket and has green required checks is squash-merged into main with no human review (review.angles = [], 0 required approvals), and since ASDLC-JA74 the item it names, if a task, is also turned into a ticket.
findings.anchor: src/tick/merge.rs pass / one (no cross_repository check before make_ticket, status writes and merge; the only fork check is at :1300, branch deletion) with .spl-asdlc/config.toml [review] angles = []
findings.evidence: Read at v1.17.0-rc.1, not reproduced live. The repository is public. A fork PR to main whose title ends `(ASDLC-XXXX)` (ticket keys are public in the commit history) resolves to that ticket through link::resolve (Livela::raw keeps it inside the project, nothing checks the PR's origin). With review.angles = [] the PR 'merges on its CI'. The required checks `required-check` and `title / conventional-title` come from GitHub Actions on `pull_request`, which runs the workflow files of the PR's merge commit, so the fork's own modified pr.yml can report them green. The only barrier left is the Actions approval for external contributors (policy all_external_contributors): once a maintainer clicks 'Approve and run', which reads as permission to run CI and not to merge, the bridge drives the ticket's status, makes a named task a ticket (ASDLC-JA74, new in this candidate), and merges outside code into main. Attacker: anyone with a GitHub account. Impact: outside code in main, which the next release cut ships to every caller, with only the release QA between them. It needs a second step (a maintainer approving the run), hence non-blocking. Obvious fix: leave cross_repository PRs out of the merge pass (as angle PRs from a fork already are), or require a coordinator's approval for them.
findings.proposed_test: tick tests: a fork PR (cross_repository) naming a project ticket, with green required checks, is neither merged nor drives its ticket's status or type, and the ticket is left as it was
